points.description: States that a queue is a data structure that stores elements (a linear collection of elements).

States precisely that elements are processed in First In First Out (FIFO) order: the first element inserted is the first removed. Must use FIFO / first in first out; a vague 'ordered' or 'line' statement is not enough.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if the idea of the earliest-added element being removed first is described but the term FIFO / first in first out is not used precisely

points.description: Names both main operations: enqueue (insert at the rear/back) and dequeue (remove from the front).
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if only one of enqueue or dequeue is named correctly

rubric.notes: Full marks need a queue defined as a data structure, the FIFO principle stated precisely, and both enqueue and dequeue named. Part marks only as stated in partial_credit. Describing a stack (LIFO), swapping the operations' meanings, or giving only a real-world analogy without the technical terms earns nothing for the affected point.
